papers.title: Complex Monge-Amp{\`e}re equations with boundary values: a variational approach
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega$ ___ C n be a bounded hyperconvex domain and $\Phi$\,: $\Omega$ $\rightarrow$ R a maximal plurisubharmonic function in $\Omega$ (possibly unbounded). We introduce a new class E 1 $\Phi$ ($\Omega$) of plurisubharmonic functions with boundary values equal to $\Phi$ in the sense of Cegrell and finite $\Phi$-energy on $\Omega$. Then given a Borel measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$, we apply a variational approach to prove that $\mu$ is the Monge-Amp{\`e}re measure of a function u $\in$ E 1 $\Phi$ ($\Omega$) if and only if it satisfies the integrability condition We also establish a quantitative version of this condition extending previous results of Cegrell and others. Using a logarithmic transformation, we obtain analogous results for the real Monge-Amp{\`e}re equations with (unbounded) boundary data.

papers.title: On the Cohomology Classes of Certain Eisenstein-Kronecker Forms
papers.abstract: We study the de Rham cohomology and Deligne splitting for a class of Eisenstein-Kronecker forms by introducing a modular weight grading. As an application, we compute a particular cohomology class that gives rise to generating series of Gromov-Witten invariants of elliptic curves.

papers.title: Operator Algebras and Their Applications
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of commutative associative algebras whose structural constants are linear operators acting in a linear topological space. An analogue of the theory of monogenic functions is developed for such algebras. It is shown that the components of monogenic functions satisfy second-order operator-differential equations. This approach provides a constructive method for obtaining solutions of various partial differential and integro-differential equations. Several illustrative examples are presented.

papers.title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
papers.abstract: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of Hayashida-Kamimoto with the help of an affine rigidity theorem in the spirit of Cartan rigidity, which should be of independent interest. For explicit angular perturbation families, we determine the full automorphism group and obtain, in particular, an abundance of examples with trivial automorphism group.

papers.title: H\"older Continuity and Boundedness of Composition Operators on Pluriharmonic $\alpha$-Bloch Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the metric properties of pluriharmonic $\alpha$-Bloch-type mappings $f=h+\overline{g}\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{B}^{n},\mathbb{C}^{n})$ on the unit ball $\mathbb{B}^{n}\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$. By synthesizing local real-part estimates with the subharmonicity of $\log(\vert{} \det Dh(z) \vert{} + \vert{} \det Dg(z) \vert{})$ along hyperbolic geodesics, we establish a globalized non-trivial lower bound across the entire unit ball $\mathbb{B}^{n}$. Using this structural decay estimate, we prove that the invariant weight quantity $D_{f}^{n,\alpha}(z)$ satisfies a global H\"older continuity estimate of order $1/n$ with respect to the Bergman metric $\beta$. Furthermore, we investigate composition operators $C_{\varphi}(f)=f\circ\varphi$ induced by holomorphic self-mappings $\varphi\in\mathcal{A}(\mathbb{B}^{n},\mathbb{B}^{n})$. We establish both sharp sufficient and necessary sampling conditions for $C_{\varphi}$ to be bounded from below on the pluriharmonic $\alpha$-Bloch space $\mathcal{B}_{P(n,\alpha)}$.

papers.title: Singular Levi-flats and holomorphic foliations on projective spaces
papers.abstract: We study codimension-one holomorphic foliations admitting invariant singular real-analytic Levi-flat varieties. Our main problem is to determine when the local meromorphic first integrals furnished by the Levi-flat geometry can be continued coherently and globalized. We introduce a pencil-singularity condition and a projective compatibility condition for local meromorphic parameters. In the projective plane these yield a characterization of foliations admitting a primitive rational first integral, while in higher-dimensional projective space they give a rational integrability criterion under a generic local-product hypothesis along the dicritical locus. We also obtain semi-global and Stein versions of these results. In a different direction, we study foliations admitting infinitely many invariant Levi-flat varieties and prove a Darboux-type alternative: either the foliation admits a rational first integral, or infinitely many Levi-flats contain a common invariant algebraic curve whose virtual holonomy is abelian. Under additional assumptions on the singularities, this leads to the existence of a closed rational, and in the absence of saddle-nodes a closed logarithmic, defining \(1\)-form.

papers.title: Asymptotic Root Dynamics under Repeated and Fractional Integration
papers.abstract: Fix a polynomial $P(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{m}a_jx^j$ of degree $m$, and let $I_kP$ be its $k$-fold antiderivative with all integration constants zero. Borwein, Chen, and Dilcher proved that, after $x=ky$, the nonzero zeros of $I_kP$ converge to the zeros of $L[P](y)=\sum_j a_j j! y^j$. That fixes a direction but neither a position nor successive differences. We compute the next two terms at a simple nonzero zero $\lambda$ of $L[P]$; these supply both. Integer-order and Riemann-Liouville integration reduce, after scaling, to one rational family $c_j(h)=\prod_{\ell\le j}(1+\ell h)^{-1}$ sampled at $h=1/k$ and $h=1/\alpha$; the scaled zero is analytic in $h$ at $h=0$. We prove $r_k=k\lambda+C_P(\lambda)+D_P(\lambda)/k+O(k^{-2})$ with explicit $C_P$ and $D_P$, whence $r_k-r_{k-1}=\lambda-D_P(\lambda)/(k(k-1))+O(k^{-3})$ and $r'(\alpha)=\lambda-D_P(\lambda)/\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{-3})$. So $\lambda$ is at once the scaled root location, the limiting discrete spacing, and the limiting continuous-order velocity, and $C_P(\lambda)$ is the offset of an asymptotic line. For binomials the limiting spacing is a multiple of a gamma-ratio quantity (the Factorial Fraction), and the nonzero reduced roots form an exact regular polygon at every positive order. For real quadratics the collision order of two branches is explicit and, under nondegeneracy hypotheses, positive exactly when $P$ has distinct real zeros and $L[P]$ has none; in arbitrary degree the collision discriminant carries a universal factor supported at negative orders, leaving a factor of degree at most $m(m-1)/2$. All trajectories form one plane curve of degree $m$ with leading form $L[P]$, whose collisions are discriminant values of the order projection and whose order-zero end is governed by a harmonic transform dual to the arithmetic one at infinity. The case $\lambda=0$ is rigid: the origin is pinned at every positive order.

papers.title: A proof of Borcea's quadratic variance conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a complex polynomial of degree $n\ge2$, and let $\sigma_2(p)$ be the root mean square distance of its zeros from their centroid, including multiplicities. We prove that every zero of $p$ lies within distance $\sigma_2(p)$ of a critical point. This proves Borcea's quadratic conjecture and, in particular, gives a new proof of Sendov's conjecture. Two polynomial integration identities prove the result analytically for $n\ge2048$. For the remaining degrees, we derive explicit necessary inequalities, including a variable integration endpoint and an exact centered coefficient identity. Directed integer arithmetic certifies a finite covering of the resulting parameter domains. Degrees $4$--$26$ use $150\,845$ certified three-dimensional regions; degrees $27$--$2047$ use a further $27\,429$ regions, with degree intervals allowed. The cases of degree 2 and 3 were already covered by Khavinson--Pereira--Putinar--Saff--Shimorin.

papers.title: Kobayashi visibility of strictly convex domains
papers.abstract: We show that any bounded strictly convex domain in $\Bbb C^N$, endowed with the Kobayashi distance, is visible.

papers.title: On the Five-Point Case of Mordell's Problem
papers.abstract: For five complex points $z_1,\ldots,z_5$ satisfying $\sum_i|z_i|^2=5$, Mordell's discriminant inequality states that $\prod_{i<j}|z_i-z_j|^2\leq5^5$, with equality precisely for a unit regular pentagon, up to rotation and permutation. We organize its proof around a direct comparison of discriminant values. A global maximizer gives a centered stationary configuration, whose coefficient equations reduce the generic case to two quartic branches. On each branch, the absolute value of a cubic polynomial gives the original discriminant objective after accounting for the normalization scale. Exact rational interval bounds exclude both branches from the maximum, and the exceptional coefficient cases leave the regular pentagon. The argument determines the maximizing configuration without reconstructing all stationary shapes. We have completed a full Lean formalization of the five-point inequality and both directions of its equality condition, including all reductions and finite checks used in this proof.

papers.title: A Counterexample to the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem
papers.abstract: In this note we show that if a contractible Stein manifold $X$ with the density property admits a proper holomorphic embedding into $\mathbb{C}^k$, then $X \times \mathbb{C}^k$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{n+k}$ with $n=\dim X$. Combined with an announced result of Auroux, Bai and Pomerleano, this shows that for some $4 \le n \le 8$ there is a complex affine variety $X$ such that $X \times \mathbb{C}$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ and $X$ is not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$. This settles the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem in the negative.

papers.title: Chern classes of Levi non-degenerate CR manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct closed Levi non-degenerate CR manifolds with non-vanishing Chern monomials. For every $n \geq 2$ and $\lceil n / 4 \rceil \leq m \leq \lfloor n / 2 \rfloor$, there exists a $(2 n + 1)$-dimensional example of signature $(\lfloor n / 2 \rfloor, \lceil n / 2 \rceil)$ on which all Chern monomials with positive indices at most $m$ and total weight at most $n - m$ are non-zero in cohomology with real coefficients. Taking $m = \lceil n / 4 \rceil$ gives examples with $c_{1}^{\lfloor 3 n / 4 \rfloor} \neq 0$. For $n = 4$ or $n \geq 6$, the latter examples show that the Chern-class vanishing theorem for strictly pseudoconvex CR manifolds does not extend to the Levi non-degenerate case. In these dimensions, their underlying manifolds admit no strictly pseudoconvex CR structures. The construction uses circle bundles over products of integral pseudo-K\"{a}hler manifolds.

papers.title: Hsiang cubics as spherical Chebyshev polynomials: equioscillation and idempotent quadrature
papers.abstract: A Hsiang cubic is a cubic form on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ whose zero set is a minimal cone; equivalently, it is the cubic form of a commutative nonassociative metrized algebra satisfying a single identity of degree four. We show that the intrinsic geometry of such an algebra, encoded in its idempotents and their Peirce decompositions, is the geometry of a Chebyshev-type extremal problem on the sphere. A Hsiang cubic equioscillates on $S^{n-1}$: its maximum set is the set of normalized idempotents, and on suitable great circles through an idempotent it restricts to the Chebyshev polynomial $T_3$. For the spherical analogue of the problem of least deviation, the minimization of $\|p\|_\infty^2/\|p\|_2^2$ over harmonic cubics, a sharp lower bound based on Kellogg's inequality shows that Cartan's isoparametric cubics are the global minimizers in dimensions $5$, $8$, $14$ and $26$. In general, we compute the ratio of every Hsiang cubic in terms of the Killing form and characterize stationarity by a Kolmogorov criterion: it amounts to a positive measure on the idempotent variety. Such measures are given explicitly in several cases which together cover every Hsiang cubic known to exist; in particular, all of them are stationary. These measures give quadrature identities on the idempotent variety whose moments are invariants of the algebra; they are spherical designs exactly in the Einstein (Killing metrized) case, i.e.\ when the Killing form is proportional to the inner product. Distinguished low-dimensional Hsiang cubics are strict local minimizers, whereas a polar Hsiang cubic is a stationary non-minimizer.

papers.title: Sharp Robertson-type coefficient estimates for radial starlike and quasi-convex of type B mappings of order {\alpha} in complex Banach spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study biholomorphic mappings $F: \mathbb{B} \to X$ of the form $F(z) = f(z)z$ for $z \in \mathbb{B}$, where $f: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{C}$ is a holomorphic function satisfying $f(0) = 1$. Our main contributions are as follows: We establish sharp estimates for the coefficients of starlike functions of order $\alpha$ as well as quasi-convex functions of type $B$ and order $\alpha$ by employing the notion of majorization. The results established here directly extend the results due to Robertson \cite{Robertson-1936} to the broader setting of complex Banach spaces.

papers.title: Holomorphic approximation for Hamiltonian diffeomorphism groups via the Symplectic Density Property
papers.abstract: We show that the cotangent bundle of a holomorphically flexible Stein manifold has the symplectic density property. As application we deduce holomorphic approximation for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of real cotangent bundles by complex symplectic automorphisms of the complexified cotangent bundles, which preserve the real bundle, in the Carleman sense, i.e. in the Whitney topology.

papers.title: The Canonical Induced Metric for Topological Branched Coverings and Geometric Applications
papers.abstract: Given a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ from a continuum-connected space into a metric space, we introduce an associated canonical pullback metric $d_f$ on $X$ by combining the target diameter structure with the Mazurkiewicz construction as \[ d_f(x,x')=\inf\{\operatorname{diam}_Y f(E): E\subset X\text{ is a continuum containing }x,x'\}. \] Our main result shows that if $f:(X,\rho)\to Y$ is $L$-BDD, then $d_f$ is quantitatively equivalent to the Mazurkiewicz metric $\rho_M$, $(d_f)_M=d_f$, every continuum satisfies $\operatorname{diam}_{d_f}E=\operatorname{diam}_Y f(E)$ and $f:(X,d_f)\to Y$ is $1$-BDD and hence $1$-BLD. For bounded-turning spaces, this identifies a canonical bi-Lipschitz metric realization in the sense that every finite-to-one topological branched covering onto a locally length metric manifold admits such a compatible induced metric without any a priori BDD hypothesis. There are two main geometric applications of the induced pullback metric. Firstly, we prove an index-free quantitative porosity theorem for branch sets and their images at points of controlled linear or inverse linear dilatation, extending the well-known Bonk-Heinonen theorem and Sarvas theorem for branch set of Euclidean quasiregular mappings to a large class of metric spaces. Secondly, we prove that every finite-to-one BDD branched covering over a doubling bounded-turning target space admits a quantitative bi-Lipschitz embedding into the target times a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. As direct corollaries, we solve several well-known open problems asked by Heinonen, Rickman and Semmes.

papers.title: The Carath\'eodory metric on Teichm\"uller space of genus two surface
papers.abstract: Let $\Tei_{g,n}$ be the Teichm\"uller space of Riemann surfaces of genus $g$ with $n$ marked points. It is conjectured that the Teichm\"uller and Carath\'{e}odory metrics coincide on a Teichm\"{u}ller disk exactly when every zero of the associated holomorphic quadratic differential (away from marked points) has even order. Gekhtman and Markovic verified this conjecture for $\Tei_{0,5}\cong \Tei_{1,2}$. We confirm the conjecture for $\Tei_{0,6}\cong\Tei_{2,0}$.

papers.title: A Transform Pair for Doubly Connected Domains
papers.abstract: A new transform-based technique that generalizes the unified transform method is developed for bounded doubly connected domains as a novel way to numerically solve boundary value problems for holomorphic functions and solutions to the Laplacian. This work builds on the transform methods for multiply connected circular domains developed by Crowdy (2015, IMA J., 80, 1902-1931) and the methods for simply connected bounded domains developed by Hulse et al. (2025, Proc. A, 481 (2319)). The Szeg\H{o} kernel of the annulus and a corresponding transformation law is pivotal in the derivation of this new technique. The modified Schwarz problem and a boundary value problem for a point vortex inside of a doubly connected domain are implemented in detail to demonstrate the effectiveness of this new method.

papers.title: Sharp weighted norm estimates for the positive Bergman operator: the two-parameter case
papers.abstract: We allow the exponent $\alpha$ that defines the positive Bergman operator on the upper half-plane to differ from the exponent $\gamma$ that defines the underlying weighted Lebesgue spaces. In this setting, we prove a sharp weak-type off-diagonal weighted inequality, with explicit and best-possible dependence on the B\'ekoll\'e--Bonami characteristic of the weight. We then deduce strong-type off-diagonal inequalities for the same operator. The key new tool is an off-diagonal extrapolation theorem, adapted to allow a change in the power of the distance to the boundary along the way.

papers.title: Sharp exponential integrability of conjugate functions
papers.abstract: We prove that if a real-valued function $f\in L^1$ on the complex unit circle has a gap of width at least $\pi$ in its essential range, then $\exp(\tilde f)$ is not integrable, where $\tilde f$ is the conjugate function. More generally, the exponential function can be replaced by any nonnegative convex function $Y$ satisfying $$ \int_0^\infty Y(x) e^{-x}\, dx = \infty. $$ We also establish a local version on arcs of the unit circle: Under a natural condition on the inverse images of the two sides of the gap, $Y(\tilde f)$ fails to be integrable on the arc; in particular, it suffices that one of these inverse images is not an interval modulo null sets. Furthermore, we obtain corresponding results for complex-valued functions and a $Y$-integrability version of Zygmund's result.
